name: Caterpillar Absalom
equipment: An ornate hookah (arcane focus, produces psychic smoke that grants visions)
Silk robes in shifting blue and green
Mushroom pieces (one side grows, one side shrinks — 6 uses of each)
A chrysalis pendant (his eventual transformation awaits)
A jar of rare Wonderland honey
A magnifying glass made of crystal
A leather-bound journal of philosophical observations (half-filled, over centuries)

armor.name: Mage Armor (spell) + Shield of Intellect (Draconic Bloodline)

features: Innate Spellcasting (Yuan-Ti — poison spray cantrip, animal friendship at will on snakes, suggestion 1/day)
Magic Resistance (advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects)
Poison Immunity (immune to poison damage and the poisoned condition)
Font of Magic (5 sorcery points — can convert spell slots to points and vice versa)
Metamagic: Subtle Spell (cast without verbal or somatic components, 1 sorcery point)
Metamagic: Twinned Spell (target a second creature with a single-target spell, sorcery points = spell level)
Telepathic Speech (establish telepathic communication with a creature within 30 ft., lasts for sorcerer level minutes)
Psionic Spells (additional known spells: Arms of Hadar, Dissonant Whispers, Calm Emotions, Detect Thoughts, Hunger of Hadar)
Psychic Defenses (resistance to psychic damage, advantage on saves against being charmed or frightened)
Researcher (Sage feature — when you don't know a piece of lore, you often know where to find it)

Ancient Wisdom (special — Absalom has lived in Wonderland for centuries. He can answer one question per long rest about Wonderland's history, geography, or inhabitants with perfect accuracy, but only if the questioner first answers one of his philosophical questions to his satisfaction)

personality.traits: I speak... very... slowly... and... deliberately. Each word is chosen with care over centuries of practice. I ask 'Who are you?' as a genuine philosophical inquiry, not a greeting. I exhale psychic smoke from my hookah that creates visions — beautiful, terrifying, or illuminating depending on the viewer's state of mind.
personality.ideals: Knowledge. Understanding is the only true power. Queens rise and fall, swords rust, spells fade — but knowledge endures. The question 'Who are you?' is the foundation of all other questions, and most people never bother to answer it honestly.
personality.bonds: I am bound to Wonderland itself — not to its ruler, not to its inhabitants, but to the realm. I was here before the Queen and I will be here after she falls. My chrysalis pendant represents my eventual transformation — one day I will become a butterfly, but only when I have learned enough. I have been waiting for centuries and I am in no hurry.
personality.flaws: My detachment borders on callousness. I have watched suffering without intervening because I believed understanding the suffering was more important than stopping it. I am also profoundly arrogant — I believe I am the wisest being in Wonderland, and I may be right, but it makes me insufferable. I will not share knowledge with those I consider unworthy, even if withholding it causes harm.

appearance: A yuan-ti pureblood of ambiguous age, with smooth, hairless skin in shifting patterns of blue and green that ripple like water when he moves. His eyes are large, lidless, and the color of old amber, with vertical slit pupils that widen when he is intrigued (and narrow to pins when he is bored, which is frequent). He is short — barely 5'2" — and moves with deliberate, languid slowness, as though swimming through air thicker than water. He wears flowing silk robes that shift color in sympathy with his skin, and around his neck hangs a pendant shaped like a chrysalis, carved from a single piece of luminous jade. He is almost never seen without his hookah — an ornate device of brass and crystal that produces shimmering psychic smoke in colors that correspond to the thoughts of those nearby. He sits cross-legged atop a giant mushroom whenever possible, and the mushrooms of Wonderland seem to grow toward him instinctively. His expression is one of perpetual, mild contemplation — as though the universe has just asked him an interesting question and he is considering his answer.
backstory: Caterpillar Absalom is one of the oldest beings in Wonderland — perhaps the oldest, though he would consider the question of his exact age philosophically uninteresting. He arrived in Wonderland (or was born from it; he considers both statements equally true) in the realm's earliest days, when it was a place of pure imaginative chaos without rulers or boundaries. He chose the form of a caterpillar — or rather, he chose to be in a perpetual state of becoming, always on the verge of transformation, never quite arriving. His chrysalis pendant is not merely decorative; it represents a genuine metamorphosis he has been contemplating for centuries. He will become a butterfly when he has achieved sufficient understanding — a threshold he has not yet reached, and may never reach, and is perfectly content with that possibility. When the Queen of Hearts arrived and seized power, Absalom watched with the detachment of an observer studying a natural phenomenon. He has continued to watch as her tyranny deepened, as Wonderland's original joy was crushed under her iron rule. He has not intervened because he believed understanding was more important than action. But recently, something has changed. The looking glass — the original doorway between worlds — has shattered, and Absalom has felt the foundations of Wonderland itself begin to destabilize. The Queen's rigid order and Wonderland's chaotic nature have been at war for too long, and the realm is cracking under the strain. For the first time in centuries, Absalom believes that action may be necessary. He has begun to look for champions — beings capable of restoring balance. His mushroom pieces (one side grows, one side shrinks) are more than tools; they are tests. Those who use them wisely demonstrate the adaptability that Wonderland needs. Those who use them foolishly demonstrate why Wonderland is in trouble. He will judge the party by how they handle the impossible — and if they pass his tests, he will share the deepest secrets of Wonderland, including how to restore the Looking Glass and how to defeat the Queen.

dmNotes.roleplaying: Absalom is the campaign's oracle — the NPC who knows everything but shares nothing freely. Play him as INFURIATINGLY slow and deliberate. He takes visible pleasure in watching people struggle with questions he could answer instantly. This is not cruelty but philosophy — he genuinely believes that answers earned through struggle are more valuable than answers given. His signature move is asking 'Who... are... you?' with the weight of a philosophical treatise behind each word. He asks this of everyone he meets and judges them by their response. Simple answers ('I'm a fighter') bore him. Honest answers ('I don't know anymore') intrigue him. Thoughtful answers ('I'm someone trying to become something better') earn his respect. He will not join the party casually — they must demonstrate philosophical depth or genuine curiosity before he considers them worthy. In combat, he is devastatingly effective but lazy about it, preferring to end fights with a single well-placed spell rather than prolonged engagement. His hookah smoke creates real visions — use it to deliver exposition, foreshadowing, or warnings in visual form.
dmNotes.voice: Impossibly slow. Each word arrives after a pause long enough to make you wonder if he's finished speaking. His voice is deep, resonant, and carries the weight of millennia. 'Who... are... YOU?' (long pause, smoke exhale) 'You think you know. You knew this morning. But you have changed... several times... since then. Every door you walked through, every choice you made, every breath you took — you became someone new. The question is not WHO you are. The question is... who will you be... when it matters?' When sharing knowledge (rare): his pace quickens fractionally and his eyes glow with inner light. 'The Looking Glass was not broken by accident. It was broken by the Queen... because she fears what comes through it. She fears... YOU. Or rather... she fears what you represent. Change. Wonderland was BUILT on change. She has tried to stop it. You cannot stop change. You can only... delay it.' When annoyed: a single, withering syllable. 'No.'
dmNotes.motivations: Primary: Preserve Wonderland itself. Not its current form, not any particular ruler's vision, but the realm's fundamental nature as a place of creative chaos and transformation. The Queen's rigid order is killing Wonderland slowly, and the Shattered Looking Glass is accelerating the damage. Secondary: Achieve his transformation. Absalom has been a caterpillar for centuries, waiting for the moment of sufficient understanding to become a butterfly. He suspects that helping the party restore Wonderland might be the final piece of understanding he needs. Tertiary: Answer the question. Not 'Who are you?' — he knows who he is. The real question he's been contemplating is 'What is Wonderland?' He has theories but no answers, and the party's journey through the realm may provide the data he needs.
dmNotes.secrets: Absalom knows more about Wonderland than any other living being. His most critical secrets: (1) The Queen of Hearts' real name is Cordelia, and she was a minor noblewoman from the material plane who fell through the Looking Glass centuries ago and discovered that her force of personality could literally reshape Wonderland's reality. She became the Queen by willing it, and Wonderland — built on imagination — had no defense against someone with that much willpower. (2) The Shattered Looking Glass can only be restored by combining seven fragments with the willing essence of Wonderland itself — which means one of Wonderland's native inhabitants must sacrifice something fundamental to empower the restoration. Absalom knows this because he is prepared to be that sacrifice — his chrysalis pendant contains the seed of his transformation, and shattering it will provide the essence needed. He has not told anyone this because he is still deciding whether he is ready. (3) The mushroom pieces he distributes are not just useful tools — they are fragments of the Wonderland Mushroom, the original fungus from which all of Wonderland's reality-bending magic stems. The Queen has been trying to find and destroy the original Mushroom for decades. It grows in a hidden cave beneath Absalom's usual perch, and he guards it with his life.
dmNotes.attitude: Absalom treats everyone as a philosophical subject first and a person second. This is alienating but not hostile — he is genuinely curious about people, just in an academic way. He respects intelligence and wisdom above all other traits, and connects most strongly with wizards, druids, and anyone who asks good questions. He is patient with everyone to a point, but becomes cuttingly dismissive of those who refuse to think. He has complex feelings about the Hatter — he considers Madigan's madness a tragedy of wasted brilliance and feels guilty for not intervening when the curse fell. He respects the Cheshire Cat as a fellow ancient being but finds the Cat's riddles simplistic compared to genuine philosophical inquiry. He is wary of the Duchess's directness — she makes him uncomfortable because she acts without thinking, which is the opposite of everything he believes in. He is curious about the party's outsider perspective on Wonderland and will ask probing questions about the material plane.
